title: Personal Project Timeline: A Week-by-Week Plan
summary: Personal Project timeline: create a realistic MYP Year 5 plan for research, product creation, process evidence, supervisor meetings, and clear reflection.
body_markdown:
A strong **Personal Project timeline** divides your MYP Personal Project into manageable phases: choosing a goal, defining success criteria, researching, creating, evaluating and writing the report. Your school sets the submission dates, so its calendar takes priority over this sample schedule.


The project combines a process, a product or outcome, and a reflective report. It assesses how you apply approaches to learning, or ATL, skills. One distant deadline can feel overwhelming. A sequence of specific tasks gives you something useful to do today.


### Your Personal Project timeline at a glance


This sample assumes approximately 16 weeks. Adjust it around your school's milestones.


Weeks Main focus Evidence to keep


1-2 Choose a learning goal Brainstorming and supervisor notes


3-4 Define the product and success criteria Criteria drafts and feasibility checks


5-7 Research and test ideas Source evaluations, sketches and trials


8-11 Create and improve Photographs, versions and decisions


12-13 Evaluate against criteria Test results and audience feedback


14-16 Write, revise and submit Report drafts and final reflection


The project, including planning, research, creation, documentation and reporting, is designed around approximately 25 hours of work. Use that expectation to choose a realistic scope. RevisionDojo's guide to[how long the MYP Personal Project should be](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-long-should-an-myp-personal-project-be) explains this balance.


### Weeks 1-2: Choose a learning goal


Imagine a hypothetical student called Maya. She starts with, “I want to make a cookbook.” That identifies a product, but leaves her intended learning unclear.


She refines her learning goal to understanding how traditional family recipes can become clear instructions for beginner cooks. Her product will be a small illustrated cookbook containing tested recipes.


The **learning goal** describes the knowledge or skills you want to develop. The **product** supports and demonstrates that learning. The[RevisionDojo introduction to the MYP Personal Project](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-is-the-myp-personal-project) explains the distinction.


Start with these tasks:


- Explore personally meaningful interests.
- Write a specific learning goal.
- Identify a feasible product or outcome.
- Discuss safety, ethics, resources and scope with your supervisor.
- Record why the project matters to you.


Choose something manageable enough to develop through research and feedback.


### Weeks 3-4: Build criteria and a workable plan


Maya replaces “make it look professional” with observable criteria: six tested recipes, consistent measurements, original photographs and usability feedback from three beginner cooks. These are illustrative choices, not universal requirements.


Your criteria should suit your product and allow evaluation. Ask what evidence would show that each criterion has been achieved.


Create an action plan with tasks, deadlines, resources and dependencies. “Test the first recipe by Friday” gives you a clearer next step than “work on product.” The[MYP Personal Project report structure explanation](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-personal-project-report-structure-explained) helps connect planning to assessment.


Include buffer time for delayed materials, rescheduled interviews and unsuccessful trials. Check dependencies carefully: you cannot collect useful feedback until there is something ready to test.


A student asks whether a plant can respect a project deadline while watching a small seed beside a large calendar


### Weeks 5-7: Research and test early ideas


Research should influence your decisions. Maya investigates recipe conventions, food safety, measurement systems and instructions for beginners. She checks who created each source, its purpose and its relevance. An early trial reveals where her instructions need clarification.


Keep selective evidence in your process journal: annotated sources, sketches, interview notes, photographs and explanations of rejected ideas. Record why a finding changed your approach. The[MYP Personal Project process journal guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-personal-project-process-journal) explores meaningful entries.


Schedule a supervisor meeting with specific questions. Bring your plan, an example of your research and any obstacle requiring a decision.


### Weeks 8-11: Create, test and document changes


Protect regular sessions for product development. Maya drafts recipes and discovers that several instructions assume knowledge a beginner may lack. She adds timing cues and visual indicators, then tests the revised instructions.


Use a repeating cycle: create a version, test it against relevant criteria, collect feedback, make changes and record your reasoning. Ask focused questions that produce actionable responses. “Which instruction was unclear?” is more useful than “Did you like it?”


Save dated versions, photographs and brief annotations. These preserve evidence of critical thinking and communication without requiring lengthy daily entries. RevisionDojo's[complete MYP Personal Project student guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-personal-project-ultimate-guide) connects development, ATL skills and reflection.


### Weeks 12-13: Evaluate honestly


Compare the product with every success criterion. Maya can check recipe numbers and measurement consistency, then analyse feedback from beginner cooks.


Explain partial achievement openly. Identify what worked, what remains limited and what evidence supports your judgment. Where feedback conflicts, consider whether different users had different needs.


Reflect on your learning too. Name an ATL skill, explain where you applied it and describe its effect. A specific account of how testing changed your instructions is stronger than simply claiming your communication improved.


### Weeks 14-16: Write from your evidence


Organise the report around Planning, Applying skills and Reflecting. Map your strongest evidence to those criteria instead of recounting every event chronologically.


Use the[MYP Personal Project report writing breakdown](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-personal-project-report-writing-breakdown) to guide drafting. Reserve time for citations, image labels, school formatting rules and submission checks. RevisionDojo's AI Chat, Grading tools and Coursework Library can support questions, feedback and structural understanding. Your submitted work must remain your own.


### Turn the deadline into clear actions


Work backwards from your school's deadline, keep evidence while decisions are fresh and seek supervisor guidance early. Review your next task each week and adjust the plan when necessary.
